newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes mostly higher on oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes mostly higher on oversold signals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed mostly higher on shortcovering tied to signals the market was oversold, traders said.
Corn futures this week had steadily fallen and new crop December was persistently notching new contract lows.
"It was oversold and due to recover," a trader said.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for the July closed at 31 percent. An RSI of 30 or less is viewed as an oversold market.
But traders remained bearish because of good crop weather in the Midwest.
"The weather is the main thing and the weather is bearish," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Warm temperatures and showers in the Midwest have led to prospects for an excellent corn crop this year, traders said.

Also long term outlooks were for the nearly ideal crop conditions to continue. The National Weather Service Thursday, in its 30 and 90 day outlooks, revealed below normal temperatures and normal rainfall for key corn growing states in the U.S.
Corn closed 1/4 cent lower to two cents higher, with July up 1/4 at $2.65-1/2 per bushel.
